intended_object: The canonical monoid homomorphism (embedding) from the multiplicative monoid of positive integers into the monoid of supernatural (Steinitz) numbers. It sends n to ∏ p^{v_p(n)}. Inferred from the docstring and from `ofPNat`.
explanation: In this library, supernatural numbers are `Multiplicative (Nat.Primes → ℕ∞)`, i.e. formal products ∏ p^{e_p} with e_p ∈ ℕ ∪ {∞}. `ofPNat n` sends the exponent at each prime p to `n.factorization p`, cast to ℕ∞. This is exactly the standard map n ↦ ∏ p^{v_p(n)}. The bundled `MonoidHom` uses the proven facts `ofPNat_one` and `ofPNat_mul`, which hold because factorization is additive on nonzero naturals. Using ℕ+ rather than ℕ is the correct domain: 0 is not a supernatural number in the standard sense, and the module docstring explicitly avoids the `factorization 0 = 0` junk convention. Mathlib has no supernatural numbers, so this neither duplicates nor restricts a more general Mathlib notion. The map is specific to its setting, so it is not too narrow.
